one_month_reasoning: No company catalyst falls in the window. Qualcomm has reported Q4 exactly 38 days after fiscal year-end three years running (FY23 to FY25), and FY26 ended Sep 27, so the print is most likely Wed Nov 4, after Oct 30 (supervisor finding; no scheduling 8-K yet). Inside the window are peer and industry reads: TSMC mid-October, Samsung preliminary results, Apple, Samsung and SK hynix late October, hyperscaler capex commentary, the Oct 28 FOMC, and possibly Counterpoint or Canalys Q3 smartphone data. Alternative data leans slightly negative for handsets: TrendForce raised its 4Q26 memory price outlook and expects DRAM tightness into 2027. That is largely known, however, and set against the September Amazon and Apple news. I have dropped the round-1 'stalled Samsung 2nm talks' explanation for the Sep 28 drop because it is unverified. Short-horizon reversal after the +23% September run and the -9% pullback roughly cancel. The ladder is therefore centred on spot (median about $184.6) with a lognormal monthly sigma of 14%, close to the 54% realized vol divided by 3.5 and slightly trimmed because the earnings gap most likely falls outside the window.

fair_value.method: 60% forward P/E (FY28 non-GAAP EPS about $11.0, which is the NTM at the horizon, x 17x = $187) and 40% FCF yield (NTM FCF about $10.5/share at a 5.7% yield, i.e. 17.5x, = $184), giving about $186 twelve months out.

inputs_detail.derivation: Multiple independent trackers agree that the handset trough runs through calendar 2027, so I assume no Android volume recovery inside FY27 and only a partial one in FY28. Samsung and Apple held up best in Q2, which cushions Snapdragon's premium mix.

Start from the $10.20 FY27 consensus. Add about $0.9 from data center growing from about $5B toward $8-9B (Amazon ramp plus the Humain 200MW AI200/AI250 programme), after the custom-silicon gross margin drag. Add about $0.2 from a 2% net share shrink from buybacks. Subtract about $0.3 for the remaining Apple modem roll-off by the Sep-2027 iPhone. That gives about $11.0, or +8%. I stay below the supervisor's $11.5 because the alt-data trackers (memory prices up again in 4Q26, handset SoC recovery only in early 2028) argue against pricing in any Android recovery before FY28, and FY27 revisions are still falling.

The stock is about 18.1x FY27 non-GAAP today ($184.5/$10.20). Handset-era non-GAAP multiples ran about 12-16x. I use 17x: a premium for the data center and auto mix, but below today's multiple because SBC is about a quarter of non-GAAP EPS and estimates are still being cut. This re-bases my round-1 18x, which was set against '20x on $9.30'.

Buybacks of about $1.4B a quarter remove about 7-8M shares a quarter. The Amazon warrant (25M at $161.26, cashless, 3.75M vested) adds about 0.5M net now and at most about 3M if fully vested.
About $11.0B FY28 FCF (modest growth from data center) divided by about 1,050M shares.
FCF is before SBC of about $3.4B a year, so a yield near 6% rather than 4-5% is appropriate. It is consistent with the 17x P/E on non-GAAP EPS.

bear.story: The memory-driven handset slump runs through 2027: TrendForce keeps raising DRAM prices, Counterpoint's early-2028 SoC recovery slips, and Qualcomm keeps losing share to MediaTek (23% in Q1 2026 vs 27%). Apple modem revenue goes to zero with the Sep-2027 iPhone. The Amazon ramp is slower than the $5B FY27 guide and no further warrant tranches vest. FY28 EPS is about $9.0 at 13.5x.

base.story: FY27 EPS lands near the $10.2 consensus, with data center about $4-5B, handsets flat to down, and automotive growing. FY28 EPS is about $11.0 as data center scales toward $8-9B and buybacks shrink the count. The multiple eases to about 17x non-GAAP.

bull.story: Data center beats the $5B target, with Amazon tranches vesting quickly, the Humain 200MW programme shipping and another hyperscaler named. Memory prices peak in H1 2027, so Android restocks early. FY28 EPS is about $12.0 and the market re-rates toward custom-silicon peers at about 22x.

thesis_break_reason: About $125 is roughly 12x the $10.20 FY27 non-GAAP consensus and just above the $121.99 52-week low. At 45-54% vol, a move to $130 is roughly one-sigma annual noise, but $125 would most likely mean something fundamental: the ~$5B FY27 data center ramp failing (Amazon or Humain programmes slipping, no further warrant tranches vesting, or the target withdrawn at the Nov 4 or February prints), or FY27 EPS heading toward $8.5-9 on a deeper memory-driven Android slump. I keep the level unchanged; the supervisor independently landed on the same one.

reasoning: Round 2 corrects three errors the supervisor found. (1) My EPS base was TIKR's undefined 'normalized' $9.30. The company-basis FY27 non-GAAP consensus is $10.20 (34 analysts), so QCOM trades at about 18x, not 20x. My round-1 FY28 of $10.50 was effectively only +3% on the right base. I rebuild FY28 at $11.0 and re-base the multiple to 17x, which leaves the P/E value roughly unchanged ($189 to $187). (2) I overstated the Amazon warrant dilution. On the treasury-stock method it is about 0.5M net shares now and at most 3M fully vested. The real share addition is Modular's 17.8M, giving a base of about 1,080M. (3) The 6.5% screen FCF yield was unnormalized. From the 8-K cash-flow statement, adding back the $1.8B inventory build (not the tax line) gives about $10.5B normalized FCF, or about $10.5/share NTM at the horizon, which at a 5.7% yield gives $184. The blend is $186, versus $188 in round 1. Following the supervisor's lane note, I replaced qualitative alt data with quantitative trackers. Counterpoint shows Q2 2026 smartphone units -11% YoY (the lowest Q2 since 2013), Omdia -4%, and IDC a record -16.7% for 2026. Counterpoint's SoC tracker puts Qualcomm's share at 23% (27% a year ago) and expects the recovery only in early 2028. TrendForce raised its 4Q26 memory price outlook and sees tightness into 2027. That is why my FY28 EPS sits below the supervisor's $11.5. Offsetting this, the premium OEMs (Samsung and Apple) outperformed, which helps Snapdragon's mix, and Humain's 200MW AI200/AI250 target gives a second data center customer beyond Amazon. I dropped the unverified Samsung 2nm explanation and the StockTwits CFO quote. Distribution: median about $186 (fair value, plus about 2% dividend not in the price), lognormal sigma 0.43 (below the event-inflated 54% realized vol, above the large-cap base rate), mixed 15% with a sigma-0.60 component to fatten both tails for the binary data center ramp. The research this round was about 8 queries; Counterpoint pages were only partly readable, so some figures come from secondary coverage of their releases.
